sources.entry: Mac Screenshot Tracker - An open source, free and hackable screenshot tracker. Re-watch what you've been working on!

summary.one_liner: A free, hackable macOS background tool that takes low-resolution screenshots at regular intervals so you can review what you worked on.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs in the background and captures low-resolution screenshots roughly every 60 seconds (the interval can be changed). A `track` command starts the capture process, and a `watch` command lets you scroll through the captured screenshots. The stated goal is to review your day and see where time was spent. The README says it is a free alternative to commercial screenshot trackers and is intentionally simple to modify. Its TODO list mentions possible future Linux and Windows support via ffmpeg, more options, and foreground-application statistics, the last of which would require PyObjC.
use_cases: track time spent on computer work
review what I worked on during the day
find out where productive time goes
free alternative to commercial screenshot trackers
record periodic screen captures on a Mac
notable: Captures low-resolution screenshots every ~60 seconds in the background
Separate track and watch commands for capture and playback
Designed to be simple and hackable
Planned ffmpeg-based Linux and Windows support (only a TODO)
caveats: Targets macOS; Linux and Windows support is only a TODO item
Requires ffmpeg to be installed separately
Foreground-app statistics are not implemented and would need PyObjC
